focus: 少說「怎麼做」，多說「為什麼」
lead: 技術決策最容易被誤解的，不是決定本身，而是只丟出結論、沒讓對方看到你怎麼權衡——沒看到取捨的人，只會覺得你在「宣布」，不是在「決定」，接下來的每一次追問都會變成質疑。今天練的是先講你放棄了什麼、為什麼放棄，再講你選了什麼——你不是在說服對方同意，你是在讓對方看懂你的判斷邏輯，即使他們最後不同意，也會相信你想清楚了。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: We ruled out X because Y — here's why it didn't make the cut.
phrases.ex: We ruled out keeping 100% density because it would've pushed turnaround past the customer's date — here's why it didn't make the cut.
phrases.gl: 先講排除的選項與理由（讓對方看到你評估過所有選項，不是只想到一個方案就拍板）

phrases.en: The trade-off we're accepting is a 1.8-point mAP gap, in exchange for a 40% cost cut.
phrases.ex: The trade-off we're accepting is a 1.8-point mAP gap, in exchange for a 40% cost cut on Ace's next batch.
phrases.gl: 把決定講成「用什麼換什麼」的交換，而不是單純的優點清單（讓對方一眼看懂你在拿什麼賭什麼）

phrases.en: This isn't the only option on the table — here's why it beat the other two.
phrases.ex: This isn't the only option on the table, David — here's why 25% beat both 50% and 100%.
phrases.gl: 承認還有其他選項存在（避免對方覺得你只想到一個方案，其他都沒比較過）

phrases.en: The number that actually drove this was 98.2%, not a guess.
phrases.ex: The number that actually drove this was 98.2% of full-density mAP on Ivy's 5,000-frame test, not a guess.
phrases.fix: 取代「I think this is probably fine」
phrases.gl: 用一個具體數字釘住決定的依據（把「我覺得」換成「這個數字」）

phrases.en: If that gap moves past three points, we revisit — that's the line.
phrases.ex: If the mAP gap moves past three points once Kevin's team retrains, we revisit — that's the line.
phrases.gl: 給決定一個「重新考慮」的明確門檻（讓決定不是死的，而是有監控機制的）

phrases.en: This decision is reversible, and here's exactly what reversing it costs.
phrases.ex: This decision is reversible, and here's exactly what reversing it costs: one extra week and Ace's standard-density rate.
phrases.gl: 講清楚決定的可逆成本（降低對方對「決定＝賭一把」的恐懼）

phrases.en: I'm not asking you to agree — I'm asking you to see the reasoning.
phrases.ex: I'm not asking you to agree yet, Kevin — I'm asking you to see the reasoning before you flag it as unsafe.
phrases.fix: 取代「Please just trust me on this」
phrases.gl: 把「說服對方同意」跟「讓對方看懂邏輯」分開（即使不同意，也會尊重你的判斷）

phrases.en: Let's separate what's decided from what's still open.
phrases.ex: Let's separate what's decided — the labeling density — from what's still open — whether fusion needs a retrain first.
phrases.gl: 把已經拍板的部分跟還在討論的部分切開講（避免整場會議變成重新辯論已決定的事）

phrases.en: Give me the number where you'd change your mind, and I'll track it.
phrases.ex: Give me the number where you'd change your mind on temporal consistency, Kevin, and I'll track it every batch.
phrases.fix: 取代「Don't worry, it'll be fine」
phrases.gl: 反問對方「什麼數字會讓你改變想法」，把抽象的擔心變成可追蹤的指標

setup: Setup. Wednesday, 3 p.m., a data-strategy review with David and two team leads. You're proposing to switch SRDC's frame-labeling strategy for the next collection cycle from dense labeling on 100% of frames to a sparse keyframe strategy — full 3D box and occlusion tagging on only 1 of every 4 frames (25% density). Ivy's internal validation on a held-out set of 5,000 frames shows the 25%-density-trained model reaches 98.2% of the full-density model's mAP, a 1.8-point gap. The change would cut vendor Ace's per-batch labeling cost by roughly 40% and shorten turnaround from ten days to six. Kevin, who leads Perception, is worried sparser labels will hurt the fusion model's temporal consistency, since his team hasn't re-trained on this format yet. Ryan manages the Ace relationship and needs a decision today to renegotiate next month's contract volume. David wants a recommendation, not just options.

prompts.frame: 先講你評估過的其他選項（50%、100%）為什麼被排除 → 用 Ivy 的數字（98.2% mAP、5,000 張held-out frame）證明 25% 已經有實證支持，不是猜測 → 承認殘留風險並給監控門檻 → 給決定的邊界條件（何時 revisit）。
prompts.model: “We actually looked at 50% first, David — it's the safer-sounding number. But at 50% we only cut Ace's cost by about fifteen percent, not forty, so it doesn't actually solve the budget problem, it just makes us feel better. Ivy ran the real test: 25% density, trained and validated on a held-out set of five thousand frames, and it hits 98.2% of the full-density model's mAP — a 1.8-point gap, not a guess. That's the number that drove this, not intuition. Here's the line: if that gap moves past three points once Kevin's team retrains on it, we revisit before the next batch, not after.”
prompts.q: David: “Why 25%? Why not something safer, like 50%, for the first cycle?”
prompts.say: 出聲講完整段（目標 45 秒）。第一句不准是「Well, actually...」，第一句要先講你排除了 50% 的原因。

prompts.frame: 承認他的風險是真的、不是無理取鬧 → 把決定拆成兩層：labeling 策略 vs fusion retrain 時程 → 提出具體驗證步驟與時間表 → 給一個測試不過的 fallback 方案。
prompts.model: “That's a fair concern, Kevin, and I don't want to wave it off — temporal consistency is exactly the piece Ivy's 5,000-frame test didn't cover. So let's separate what's decided from what's still open. What's decided: Ace switches to 25% density starting next batch, because the cost and mAP numbers already justify that on their own. What's still open: whether your fusion model needs retraining before it touches that data in production. Give me the number where you'd change your mind — if temporal consistency drops more than two points on your own validation set, I'll hold the sparse-labeled batch out of production and we go back to 100% for fusion-critical data only.”
prompts.q: Kevin: “My team hasn't validated fusion temporal consistency on sparse labels — I don't think we should ship this yet.”
prompts.say: 出聲練習「不要用『別擔心』開場」。禁用 “don't worry”、“it'll be fine”。

prompts.frame: 先給明確決定（不用 modal 語氣）→ 講清楚這個決定基於什麼證據，不是臨時起意 → 給一個 reversible 的安全閥（revisit 條件）→ 明確授權 Ryan 去談。
prompts.model: “Confirmed — 25% density, starting next batch, go ahead and lock the volume with Ace. This isn't a trial we're hoping works out: Ivy already validated it at 98.2% of full-density mAP on five thousand held-out frames, and it cuts their labeling cost by roughly forty percent, which is exactly the number Finance asked us to hit this quarter. It is reversible — if Kevin's fusion retrain shows more than a two-point drop in temporal consistency, we go back to 100% for fusion-critical batches only, and I'll tell you within a week if that's happening. For now, tell Ace twenty-five percent, six-day turnaround, and lock it.”
prompts.q: Ryan: “Ace needs an answer today to lock next month's volume — can you confirm 25%?”
prompts.say: 練習「直接給答案，不要拖泥帶水」。禁用 “I think we can probably”、“let's just try”。

fixes.good: We've decided to go with 25% density.
fixes.note: Grammar（時態）：decide 這個動作已經完成，要用現在完成式（have decided）或過去式，不能用現在簡單式描述一個已經做完的決定。

fixes.bad: This decision base on the data from Ivy.
fixes.good: This decision is based on the data from Ivy.
fixes.note: Grammar（be 動詞遺漏）：base on 是動詞片語，被動用法一定要有 be 動詞（is based on），不能省略 be 直接寫 base on。

fixes.bad: I think maybe this is better, but I'm not sure.
fixes.good: This is the option I'd recommend, and here's why.
fixes.note: Register（語氣強度）：think / maybe / not sure 三個緩衝詞疊在一起，會讓決定聽起來像猶豫不決，削弱 PM 該有的判斷力可信度。

fixes.bad: The risk is depend on how much Kevin's team retrain.
fixes.good: The risk depends on how much retraining Kevin's team does.
fixes.note: Grammar（動詞形態）：depend on 前面不需要 be 動詞，直接用 depends；retrain 在這裡要轉成名詞 retraining，且動詞要接在正確位置（does the retraining）。

fixes.bad: This option is more good than the 50% one.
fixes.good: This option is better than the 50% one.
fixes.note: Grammar（比較級）：good 的比較級是 better，是不規則變化，不能用 more good 這種規則變化去硬套。

challenge:
今天做任何技術或流程決定時做這一件事：先講「你排除了什麼」，再講「你選了什麼」——

“Before I tell you what we're doing — here's what we ruled out, and why. Then here's the call: ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑一件你這週已經做但還沒好好講清楚的決定，重講一次。

  • 第一句要先講「排除了什麼」，不能先講「決定是什麼」
  • 中段要有一個具體數字支撐這個決定（百分比、天數、次數）
  • 結尾要講清楚「什麼情況下會重新考慮這個決定」
  • 禁用：I think maybe、probably、it should be fine、let's just try、whatever works
check: 我今天講決定的時候，有沒有先講「排除了什麼」，還是直接跳到結論？
我有沒有用具體數字支撐這個決定，還是只講「感覺比較好」？
我有沒有講清楚這個決定在什麼條件下會被重新檢視，還是講得像永遠不會變？
